title: Group: legal entity register and organization charts
source_system: Corporate secretary's entity management system
what_it_shows: A publicly traded holding company (SEC registrant) with three wholly owned operating subsidiaries: Meat Processing, Food Distribution and Grocery Retail. Corporate shared services (identity, network, security operations, cloud and data platform, group ERP, OT security services, HR, finance, legal and internal audit) sit in the parent. Organization charts show the Group CISO, the Group OT security director reporting to the Group CISO, three division security and compliance leads, and group internal audit reporting to the board audit committee

title: Group: HR roster by division and plant
source_system: Group HR SaaS
what_it_shows: 45,000 employees: Meat Processing about 14,000 (Plant 1 about 3,000, Plant 2 about 2,200, Plant 3 about 2,600, Plant 4 about 2,400, Plant 5 about 1,800, Plant 6 about 2,000), Food Distribution about 7,000, Grocery Retail about 21,000 and corporate shared services about 3,000. Agency temporary workers are listed by staffing agency. Termination events feed SYS-G1 identity governance

title: Group: FY2025 revenue by division
source_system: ERP general ledger (SYS-G4); FY2025 Form 10-K segment note
what_it_shows: Revenue of about $18.0 billion: Meat Processing about $7.0 billion in external sales over about 250 production days (intercompany sales to Food Distribution eliminated), Food Distribution about $5.0 billion and Grocery Retail about $6.0 billion, of which online orders are about 9%. About 30% of Meat Processing volume moves through the group's DCs, and about 40% of the stores' fresh and deli meat comes from the group's plants

title: Group: applicability questionnaire response from group legal
source_system: Group legal (contract system and regulatory affairs files)
what_it_shows: No federal contracts or subcontracts in any division; no MTSA-regulated facility; no business in California; no in-store pharmacies; no child-directed online services; no online marketplace for third-party sellers; no Protected Critical Infrastructure Information has been submitted to DHS. The co-branded credit card is issued by a partner bank, and Grocery Retail extends no credit itself

title: Group: SEC cybersecurity disclosure and disclosure committee charter
source_system: SEC filings (FY2025 Form 10-K Item 1C); corporate secretary
what_it_shows: The FY2025 Form 10-K includes the Reg S-K Item 106 description. It describes the group policies, the SOC and board oversight, and does not describe plant OT or division programs. The disclosure committee charter includes cybersecurity materiality decisions

title: Group: security policies (2025) and policy register
source_system: Group policy repository
what_it_shows: Group security policies aligned to NIST CSF 2.0, approved in 2025. The policy register lists the division documents: the Meat Processing supplement v2025 (aligned 2025-10), the Food Distribution security standards v2023 (dated 2023-04, with no named owner or review date) and the Grocery Retail supplement, maintained with the PCI DSS program

title: Group: common control catalog (2025) and inheritance records
source_system: Group GRC tool
what_it_shows: 82 common controls with their providers (SYS-G1, SYS-G2, SYS-G3, SYS-G5, SYS-G6, group governance and group HR). Inheritance is recorded for Meat Processing (2025 inheritance matrix; SYS-G5 coverage limited to Plants 1, 3, 4 and 6) and for Grocery Retail (the PCI DSS responsibility matrix in the 2025 ROC). No Food Distribution inheritance matrix was provided

title: Group: SYS-G1 authentication and sign-in policy export
source_system: Group identity platform admin console (SYS-G1)
what_it_shows: 45,000 workforce identities. MFA is required for all workforce access to IT systems, with number matching; administrators and OT engineers use phishing-resistant authenticators; accounts lock after 10 failed attempts; sign-in banners are configured; identifiers are assigned from HR records and are not reused

title: Group: identity governance and PAM exports
source_system: SYS-G1 identity governance and PAM consoles
what_it_shows: Joiner, mover and leaver workflows run from HR events; quarterly access certification covers IT applications (the Q1 2026 campaign is complete); accounts inactive for 60 days are disabled automatically; privileged IT and OT engineering access is granted just in time through PAM with session recording, and PAM sessions are logged to the SIEM. The service account register lists 34 privileged directory service accounts that are not vaulted in PAM and not in certification campaigns

title: Group: corporate directory domain membership and restore records
source_system: Corporate directory (SYS-G1) domain controllers
what_it_shows: Domain controllers run in the colocation data center and at each plant and DC. OT servers at Plants 2 and 5 (SCADA, historians and MES), the DC automation servers at all five DCs and the store back-office servers are joined to the corporate domain. Plants 1, 3, 4 and 6 run a separate OT domain. The last directory restore test on record (from offline system-state backups) is from 2025

title: Group: SIEM data source inventory and EDR coverage report
source_system: SIEM and EDR consoles (SYS-G2)
what_it_shows: 24x7 SOC. EDR runs on all IT servers, endpoints and cloud hosts, including DC automation Windows servers, and on OT Windows hosts at Plants 1, 3, 4 and 6. OT monitoring feeds come from Plants 1, 3, 4 and 6 and from DC-1 and DC-3, and none from Plants 2 and 5 or DC-2, DC-4 and DC-5. No cold-chain platform source is listed. WMS and DC automation logs are not forwarded. Account behavior analytics cover interactive users. Data loss prevention rules cover email only

title: Group: SOC case records and incident tickets, April 2025 to March 2026
source_system: SOC case management system
what_it_shows: Incidents are tracked in the case system under the group severity scale; Food Distribution cases carry the division's own three-level DC scale. Daily triage of high-severity events and weekly reviews of privileged activity are recorded, as are alerts on logging and EDR failures

title: Group: incident response plan v4, SOC playbooks and exercise reports
source_system: SOC document library
what_it_shows: Incident response plan v4 is dated 2025-11-30. The playbooks include OT ransomware; the OT playbook has no product hold step and does not route a product question to FSQA. Exercise reports show IT playbooks tested each quarter; no exercise included a plant product hold or an FSIS notice decision. Payment card incident steps sit in the Grocery Retail program documents

title: Group: draft multi-regulator notification matrix
source_system: Group legal
what_it_shows: The matrix is a draft listing food regulator, state breach, card brand and SEC notice duties by division. It does not list 3PL customer or independent grocer notice terms. No exercise of the matrix is recorded

title: Group: vulnerability scan, patch and passive OT matching reports
source_system: Vulnerability scanner, patch console and SYS-G5 OT monitoring console
what_it_shows: Weekly IT vulnerability scans and IT patch compliance reports; passive OT vulnerability matching at Plants 1, 3, 4 and 6 and DC-1 and DC-3; no scan or passive matching results for OT at Plants 2 and 5

title: Group: cloud account inventory, IAM roles and guardrail compliance report
source_system: Cloud consoles and guardrail policy service (SYS-G3, providers A and B)
what_it_shows: Provider A hosts the corporate landing zone, the group data platform, SYS-M5, the recipe master library and SYS-D3; provider B hosts SYS-R2, the DR replicas and the immutable backup vault. Cloud roles are federated from SYS-G1, division accounts receive division roles only, and break-glass roles are sealed. Mandatory guardrail policies (encryption, logging, no public storage) and an allowed-services list apply to every division account. Provider DDoS protection is enabled on the SYS-M5, recipe library, SYS-D3 and SYS-R2 endpoints

title: Group: landing-zone and colocation firewall policies and private link inventory
source_system: Firewall management and network inventory (SYS-G3)
what_it_shows: Hub firewalls and private endpoints; deny by default between division accounts and between the hub and the colocation link; no direct internet path from division workloads. Private links to the colocation data center, 6 plants, 5 DCs and 120 stores are encrypted with IPsec, with cellular failover at every store and DC. Plants 3 and 4 each have a single WAN carrier

title: Group: external TLS scan of group endpoints
source_system: TLS scanner (SYS-G2)
what_it_shows: The endpoints for SYS-M5, the recipe master library, SYS-D3, SYS-R2, the store links to the payment processor and the SYS-G6 integrations accept TLS 1.2 or higher only

title: Group: key management and encryption settings
source_system: Key management services (providers A and B)
what_it_shows: Key policies and rotation per account; customer-managed keys for the SYS-M5, recipe library, SYS-D3 and SYS-R2 data stores; storage and backups encrypted at rest

title: Group: immutable backup vault configuration, backup and restore reports, and DR runbooks
source_system: Backup vault (provider B); cloud DR runbooks
what_it_shows: Immutable daily backups of provider A workloads in provider B under a separate backup identity; quarterly restore tests of cloud datasets are on record. SYS-M5 and the recipe library replicate to provider B for failover; the last SYS-M5 failover exercise on record is from 2025

title: Group: central log archive configuration and time sources
source_system: Log archive account and network time service (SYS-G3)
what_it_shows: Write-once log archive in a separate account that division administrators cannot delete from; retention 1 year searchable and 6 years archived. IT and OT clocks synchronize to group time sources, through the OT DMZ at Plants 1, 3, 4 and 6 and directly through the domain at Plants 2 and 5

title: Group: security standards library and 2026 roadmap
source_system: Group policy repository
what_it_shows: Logging standard with an OT addendum (setpoint, recipe, alarm acknowledgment, sign-in and historian edit events); OT reference architecture (zones and conduits, OT DMZ, separate OT domain); OT remote access standard (SYS-G5 only); continuous monitoring plan; key, endpoint, workstation and removable media policies; procurement security templates; supplier and vendor access procedures; the tailoring register (for example, HMI lockout tailored out). The 2026 roadmap lists a criticality analysis of components that act on food and annual OT and cold-chain supplier reviews as planned

title: Group: SYS-G5 OT remote access gateway configuration, account list and session logs
source_system: SYS-G5 gateway console (colocation data center)
what_it_shows: Deployed for Plants 1, 3, 4 and 6 and for DC-1 and DC-3; not deployed for Plants 2 and 5 or for DC-2, DC-4 and DC-5. Named engineer and vendor accounts with MFA, session approval and recording; sessions encrypted end to end; session logs for January to March 2026 on file

title: Group: SYS-G5 passive OT monitoring asset reports
source_system: SYS-G5 OT monitoring console
what_it_shows: About 1,450 OT devices inventoried at Plants 1, 3, 4 and 6; DC-1 and DC-3 automation and freezer controls inventoried; no sensors at Plants 2 and 5 or at DC-2, DC-4 and DC-5

title: Group: SYS-G6 cold-chain platform configuration and sensor inventory
source_system: Cold-chain monitoring SaaS admin console (SYS-G6)
what_it_shows: About 21,000 sensors: plant coolers, freezers and docks (about 4,300), DC rooms, refrigerated trailers through trailer telematics, and store cases and walk-ins. Alerts reach site on-call roles by SMS and app push through one alert integration server in the colocation data center. Gateways at DCs and stores sit on general DC and store networks, and at Plants 2 and 5 on the business network. Gateways buffer readings for 24 hours. No alert feed to the SIEM is configured

title: Group: cold-chain alert integration server DR runbook and test history
source_system: Group cold-chain services document library
what_it_shows: The DR runbook is a draft; it rebuilds the server from code. No failover test of the server is recorded. Manual temperature log procedures exist at plants, DCs and stores

title: Group: cold-chain vendor file
source_system: Group third-party risk tool
what_it_shows: SaaS contract with group security terms added in 2025; the vendor holds the monitoring records; the last recorded review of the vendor's SOC 2 report is from 2024; a request for the current report was opened on 2026-04-13

title: Group: accounts payable vendor master and third-party risk register
source_system: ERP vendor master (SYS-G4); group third-party risk tool
what_it_shows: Tiered vendor program. Annual SOC 2 reviews are recorded for the cloud providers, the identity vendor, the ERP vendor and the WMS vendor. No review is recorded for the trailer telematics vendor, the DC automation vendor, the Plants 2 and 5 controls integrator or the refrigeration contractors. Also listed: the AI vision inspection vendor, the camera analytics vendor (no security review recorded), the MES vendor, the e-commerce and loyalty platform vendors, the payment processor and P2PE solution provider, the QSA firm, three delivery partners, the EDI network provider, carriers, the colocation provider, staffing agencies, the cyber insurer and the forensic firm on the insurer's panel

title: Group: vendor SOC 2 reports on file
source_system: Vendor portals (cloud providers A and B, identity SaaS vendor, ERP vendor, WMS vendor)
what_it_shows: SOC 2 Type 2 reports for cloud providers A and B (including physical access and media sanitization at provider facilities), the identity SaaS vendor, the ERP vendor (vendor backups with a 1-hour RPO by contract) and the WMS vendor

title: Group: ERP (SYS-G4) contract and role certification records
source_system: ERP admin console; legal contract system
what_it_shows: The ERP runs finance, procurement, order-to-cash and production orders for all divisions; group roles are certified each quarter for all division users; the contract sets vendor backups with a 1-hour RPO

title: Group: learning system training and acknowledgment reports
source_system: Group learning management system
what_it_shows: Annual security awareness for all workforce, with a short module for plant hourly staff at hire and each year; email filtering and quarterly phishing exercises; acceptable use acknowledged at hire and each year; the role training catalog includes an OT security module and food defense modules; incident response training is recorded for SOC analysts and division liaisons and not for plant FSQA managers

title: Group: HR screening, termination and sanctions procedures and records
source_system: Group HR system; HR policy library
what_it_shows: Background checks for roles with access to formulations, OT engineering, the food defense plan or the cardholder data environment; the termination procedure disables SYS-G1 accounts within 4 hours and badges the same day; a sanctions log is kept under the group procedure

title: Group: board committee minutes and risk acceptance records, 2025 to 2026
source_system: Board portal; group GRC tool
what_it_shows: The board risk committee receives quarterly cyber and food safety risk reports; the board audit committee oversees group internal audit; risk acceptances are recorded by level (division lead, division president, Group Chief Risk Officer with the Group CISO, board risk committee)

title: Group: 2025 risk registers and risk management strategy
source_system: Group GRC tool
what_it_shows: The 2025 group and division risk registers and the group risk management strategy with acceptance authority by level; the register change log records changes by date

title: Group: cyber insurance policy
source_system: Group risk management
what_it_shows: Cyber insurance in force for 2026, with a breach hotline and a forensic panel

title: Group: records retention schedule
source_system: Group records management
what_it_shows: Security policies, risk analyses, assessments and incident records are kept 6 years; CCP records follow 9 CFR 417.5(e); food defense records are kept 3 years

title: Group: AI tool discovery
source_system: Procurement records; SaaS discovery and SYS-G1 app list; data platform model registry
what_it_shows: AI in use: AI vision inspection on 7 packaging lines at Plants 1, 3 and 4 (in production since 2025); a predictive maintenance model for ammonia refrigeration compressors at Plants 1, 3 and 6 on the group data platform; WMS and ERP demand forecasting; TMS route optimization; store loss-prevention camera analytics at 12 stores since 2026-04-06; personalized loyalty offers; a workforce scheduling engine; and an enterprise generative AI assistant piloted with 1,500 workforce users. The forecasting and routing tools are not recorded in any AI register

title: Group: HR data stores and data loss prevention configuration
source_system: File share permissions report; data loss prevention console
what_it_shows: HR file shares and payroll exports hold names, Social Security numbers and bank details for the 45,000 employees and for former employees; access is limited to HR; data loss prevention rules cover email only

title: Group: threat intelligence and advisory distribution records
source_system: SOC threat intelligence platform
what_it_shows: The SOC receives food and agriculture sector threat information and CISA ICS advisories, and distributes OT indicators and advisories to plant controls engineers

title: Group: endpoint and mobile device management reports, software register and disposal records
source_system: Endpoint management console; software asset register; IT asset disposal records
what_it_shows: Users cannot install software on managed endpoints; mobile devices used for alerts and engineering are enrolled in device management; a licensed software register is kept, and OT software is issued through engineering; IT asset disposal certificates are on file

title: Group: interconnection register
source_system: Group GRC tool
what_it_shows: Interconnection records exist for the ERP, WMS, SYS-G6 and SYS-M5 links. No records exist for the controls integrator connections at Plants 2 and 5 or the AI vision vendor connection at Plant 3

title: Meat Processing: plant register and FSIS grants of inspection
source_system: Division regulatory affairs files
what_it_shows: Six further-processing plants with no slaughter: Plant 1 (Florida) bacon, hams, smoked sausage and deli meats; Plant 2 (acquired 2024) fresh sausage and ground products; Plant 3 cooked meats for food service; Plant 4 marinated and case-ready cuts; Plant 5 (acquired 2024) smoked sausage and meat snack sticks; Plant 6 deli meats plus a plant-based protein line opened in 2024. Each plant holds a federal grant of inspection as an FSIS official establishment

title: Meat Processing: FDA food facility registration records
source_system: FDA registration account (Unified Registration and Listing System)
what_it_shows: Plant 6 is registered as a food facility because its plant-based line makes FDA-regulated food. Plants 1 to 5 are not registered. Plant 6's renewal falls in the 2026 window (2026-10-01 to 2026-12-31)

title: Meat Processing: OT network drawings and firewall exports, all six plants
source_system: Plant firewall management; OT documentation
what_it_shows: Plants 1, 3, 4 and 6: zone and conduit drawings, an OT DMZ with brokered one-way historian replication to SYS-M5 and the ERP, deny-by-default rules between zones, and a separate OT domain. Plants 2 and 5: flat IT and OT networks with broad firewall rules and direct connections to SYS-M5 and the ERP, and no zone drawings. Cold-chain gateways at Plants 2 and 5 sit on the business network

title: Meat Processing: OT device counts and Plants 2 and 5 asset spreadsheets
source_system: OT documentation; 2024 acquisition asset spreadsheets
what_it_shows: About 2,100 OT devices (PLCs, brine and cure dosing skids, smokehouse and oven controllers, CIP manifolds, chilling, slicing, packaging, metal detectors and checkweighers) and 310 HMIs across six plants. The Plants 2 and 5 inventories are 2024 spreadsheets. 24 HMIs at Plants 2 and 5 run an operating system past its vendor's support end date

title: Meat Processing: HMI, MES and recipe library account and role exports
source_system: Plant MES consoles; HMI configuration; recipe master library (SYS-G3)
what_it_shows: HMIs at all six plants use shared operator logins, which carry supervisor rights at Plants 2 and 5. MES at Plants 1, 3, 4 and 6 uses named accounts with two-person formulation approval (approval logs since 2025); MES at Plants 2 and 5 uses shared logins. PLC key switches and engineering roles limit logic and formulation changes at four plants. Recipe library author and approver roles are separate; library administrators are cloud platform administrators. Engineering workstations lock after 10 minutes idle

title: Meat Processing: historian and SYS-M5 audit and role configuration
source_system: Plant historians; SYS-M5 admin console
what_it_shows: Historian audit trails are enabled and protected at Plants 1, 3, 4 and 6 and disabled at Plants 2 and 5; MES records are append-only. SYS-M5 keeps the original value, user and time on every edit, plant users cannot delete records, plant-level and FSQA approval roles are configured, and the shared administrator account was removed in 2025. Pre-shipment review at Plants 2 and 5 is signed with typed initials; the SYS-M5 release plan lists electronic signatures as planned

title: Meat Processing: OT backup reports, PLC program repository and restore records
source_system: Plant backup consoles; PLC program repository
what_it_shows: Plants 1, 3, 4 and 6: OT backups copied offline weekly, a PLC program repository with a monthly comparison of running programs, quarterly restore tests on record, and recovery runbooks that verify formulations against signed masters before restart. Plants 2 and 5: nightly backups to domain-joined storage in the same server room, no restore test on record, and PLC programs kept on engineering laptops

title: Meat Processing: OT change records 2025 to 2026 and change procedure
source_system: Division change management system
what_it_shows: Change control at Plants 1, 3, 4 and 6 includes an FSQA HACCP impact check and no food defense step. The 2025 Plant 6 MES upgrade (a new recipe release path and remote engineering access) was approved with a HACCP check and has no food defense reanalysis record. At Plants 2 and 5 the integrator records changes in its own system, with no HACCP check and no integrity check record for its software updates

title: Meat Processing: OT patch, allowlisting and removable media reports
source_system: Plant patch and allowlisting consoles
what_it_shows: At Plants 1, 3, 4 and 6, OT patches go through change control after vendor approval, application allowlisting runs on HMIs and SCADA hosts, and removable media is blocked on OT hosts (with scanning kiosks at Plants 1 and 3). There are no OT patch, allowlisting or removable media records for Plants 2 and 5. The 2027 capital plan lists replacement of the 24 unsupported HMIs

title: Meat Processing: remote access path inventory
source_system: Plant firewall rules; OT documentation
what_it_shows: Plants 2 and 5: the controls integrator uses one shared VPN account, always on and without MFA, which the firewall allows to the SCADA subnet. Plant 5: a refrigeration contractor keeps an always-on cellular modem on the refrigeration controller. Plants 1, 3 and 4: the AI vision vendor's remote tool runs always on on the edge inference servers

title: Meat Processing: OT supplier and staffing contracts
source_system: Legal contract system
what_it_shows: The legacy controls integrator contract for Plants 2 and 5 and the Plant 5 refrigeration contractor's service contract contain no security terms; one small integrator serves both plants. The AI vision vendor contract has no image retention or reuse terms. Staffing agency contracts require agency workers to follow group rules

title: Meat Processing: ammonia refrigeration and PSM register
source_system: Plant PSM program files
what_it_shows: Plants 1, 2, 3, 5 and 6 hold about 38,000, 22,000, 30,000, 14,000 and 26,000 lb of anhydrous ammonia; Plant 4 uses a low-charge packaged system below the 10,000 lb threshold. The DC-1 and DC-3 freezers also hold ammonia above the threshold. Ammonia detector tests are tracked on paper

title: Meat Processing: HACCP plans, Sanitation SOPs and recall procedures, all six plants
source_system: Division FSQA document system
what_it_shows: Each plant's HACCP plans list CCPs (including cook, chill and cold storage temperatures), monitoring procedures and frequencies, corrective actions and recordkeeping. The unforeseen-deviation procedure assumes a single-plant outage. Annual reassessment records exist at every plant. The written recall procedure includes the 24-hour FSIS notice, and mock recall reports show one per plant each year. Pre-shipment review and FSIS records access procedures are written. Lot data sits in MES, the WMS and store systems under different keys

title: Meat Processing: plant contingency plans, all six plants
source_system: Division continuity library
owner: Meat Processing security and compliance lead
what_it_shows: Each plan is tied to the plant's HACCP corrective actions and describes a single-plant outage; none has a post-restore label verification step. The Plants 2 and 5 plans carry pre-acquisition dates

title: Meat Processing: Plant 6 food defense plan (2024) and vulnerability assessment
source_system: Plant 6 FSQA document system
what_it_shows: Written plan for the plant-based line, prepared in 2024 and signed and dated by the Plant 6 plant manager. The roles page names the Plant 6 FSQA manager as qualified individual and assigns responsibility in writing; the scope statement covers the plant-based process and claims no exemption for processing steps. The vulnerability assessment worksheets cover receiving, blending, brining, forming, cooking and packaging, with public health impact for each step; automated brine dosing, CIP valve control and recipe setpoints are evaluated for physical access only, and access through HMIs, MES and the recipe library is outside the assessment. Mitigation strategies are written for physical steps (locks, CCTV, seals). Monitoring, corrective action and verification procedures are written; verification lists records review only. The plan history shows no revision after the 2025 MES upgrade. The plan is a controlled record and a copy is also stored on a site share readable by plant office staff

title: Meat Processing: food defense training and qualification records
source_system: Learning system; Plant 6 FSQA files; staffing agency records
what_it_shows: The Plant 6 FSQA manager completed FDA-recognized intentional adulteration training and the vulnerability assessment course (certificates on file). Employees receive food defense awareness training at hire; agency workers are trained in their first week, and the agency holds their training records

title: Meat Processing: AI vision inspection (SYS-M6) configuration
source_system: SYS-M6 vendor dashboard; plant OT documentation
what_it_shows: In production on 7 lines since 2025 (Plant 1: 3; Plant 3: 2; Plant 4: 2). Edge inference servers sit on the line control networks, on a separate VLAN at Plants 1 and 3; model training runs in the vendor cloud. Divert dispositions are recorded in SYS-M5 at Plants 1 and 3 and in the vendor dashboard at Plant 4. The cameras have no microphones

title: Meat Processing: plant physical security, maintenance and generator records
source_system: Badge system; CCTV system; visitor logs; maintenance management system
what_it_shows: Plant managers approve badge authorizations for production floors, engine rooms, brine rooms and server rooms; entries are guarded; CCTV covers docks, ingredient rooms, brine rooms and engine rooms and is reviewed after alarms; visitor logs show integrator staff working unescorted after hours at Plants 2 and 5; PLC and CCP instrument maintenance and calibration are on schedule; standby generators for refrigeration, SCADA and server rooms hold about 72 hours of fuel

title: Meat Processing: division file share permissions
source_system: File share permissions report
owner: Meat Processing security and compliance lead
what_it_shows: Formulation sheets on division file shares are readable by all plant office staff

title: Meat Processing: recipe master library configuration and audit log
source_system: Recipe master library admin console (SYS-G3)
what_it_shows: Every formulation change is logged; releases are signed, and plant MES verifies the signature before loading; no change alert to plant FSQA is configured; the library replicates to provider B; signed paper formulation masters are kept at each plant

title: Food Distribution: DC register, FDA registrations and FSIS registration
source_system: Division regulatory and facilities files
what_it_shows: Five DCs with ambient, refrigerated and frozen storage, holding food in packaged form only and with no liquid storage tanks; all five are registered with FDA, with renewals scheduled for the 2026 window and an owner assigned. The division is registered with FSIS as a meat wholesaler and public warehouseman; the registration file lists DC-5's previous office address (DC-5 moved its office in 2025). Transaction data is captured in the ERP and the WMS. DC-1 and DC-3 have badge access, CCTV and standby generators with test logs; the DC-1 hurricane plan uses DC-3 for overflow

title: Food Distribution: security standards v2023
source_system: Group policy repository
owner: Food Distribution security and compliance lead
what_it_shows: Standards dated 2023-04 with no named owner or review date. They set 30-day retention for WMS and automation logs, next-business-day termination, vendor remote tools allowed with a firewall rule, a three-level DC incident severity scale and monthly temperature record review. They do not address common control inheritance or AI use

title: Food Distribution: WMS and DC automation configuration
source_system: WMS admin console (SYS-D1); DC automation server consoles
what_it_shows: One WMS tenant serves all five DCs, with accounts federated to SYS-G1; pre-cool checks are recorded at the dock door. DC-1 and DC-3 run conveyors, sortation and automated freezer storage. DC automation servers at all DCs are joined to the corporate domain; an OT DMZ exists at DC-1 and DC-3 only. Automation servers back up nightly to domain-joined storage, with no restore test on record. WMS and automation logs are kept 30 days. The automation vendor uses its own remote tool at DC-2, DC-4 and DC-5. OT inventories at DC-2, DC-4 and DC-5 are spreadsheets. WMS lot keys differ from MES lot codes. At two DCs, inventory adjustments are approved by the supervisor who requests them

title: Food Distribution: TMS and trailer telematics configuration and account list
source_system: TMS (SYS-D2) and telematics vendor portal
what_it_shows: About 450 tractors and 900 refrigerated trailers, all with telematics and on a reefer preventive maintenance program. Setpoints are sent from the TMS to the reefers; telematics reports setpoints and temperatures to SYS-G6 and raises alerts. Dispatchers sign in to the telematics portal with shared logins. Temperature history is kept 90 days in the portal; the vendor holds 2 years of location data

title: Food Distribution: refrigerated storage records
source_system: SYS-G6 exports; DC paper logs
what_it_shows: A room setpoint register defines setpoints and alarm limits for every refrigerated and frozen room; SYS-G6 exports show continuous monitoring; the DC rooms have no alarm path independent of SYS-G6. The written corrective action procedure covers equipment failures and does not mention loss of monitoring from a cyber incident. The vendor checks sensors against a reference each quarter, with calibration certificates and review sign-offs. Review logs show weekly reviews at DC-1 and DC-3 and monthly reviews at DC-2, DC-4 and DC-5. Corrective action and verification records are on paper at DC-2, DC-4 and DC-5

title: Food Distribution: sanitary transportation program (2021) and dispatch procedures
source_system: Division document system
what_it_shows: Integrated written procedures (2021) assign roles for each DC and the fleet and name the division food safety manager and the fleet director in writing. Written specifications go with every third-party load; dispatch requires pre-cool; drivers and dispatch escalate reefer alarms; receivers record probe and reefer readings. The procedures do not address telematics or monitoring outages or loads with missing telematics data. Driver training at hire and each year is recorded in the learning system, and program records are kept in the document system

title: Food Distribution: 3PL service and customer agreements
source_system: Legal contract system; 3PL account management
what_it_shows: About 60 external brands store refrigerated and frozen product at DC-1 and DC-3 under agreements on four contract versions, with differing service commitments and incident notice terms. 14 of them, including two national food manufacturers, asked for a SOC 2 report by the end of 2027 covering Security, Availability and Processing Integrity. Independent grocer supply agreements include notice terms. 3PL customer communications are kept in the account files

title: Food Distribution: 3PL customer portal (SYS-D3) and EDI configuration
